definitions.explanation: The resistance encountered when surfaces move against each other (physics).
Disagreement or tension between people, groups, or nations (figurative).

examples.japanese: {摩擦|まさつ}で{熱|ねつ}が{出|で}る。
{手|て}を{摩擦|まさつ}すると{温|あたた}かくなる。
examples.english: Rubbing your hands together makes them warm.

examples.japanese: {摩擦|まさつ}を{減|へ}らすために{油|あぶら}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Oil is used to reduce friction.

examples.japanese: {貿易|ぼうえき}{摩擦|まさつ}が{問題|もんだい}だ。
{職場|しょくば}での{摩擦|まさつ}を{避|さ}ける。
examples.english: To avoid friction in the workplace.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}の{間|あいだ}に{長|なが}い{間|あいだ}{摩擦|まさつ}があったが、{最近|さいきん}は{関係|かんけい}が{改善|かいぜん}してきた。
examples.english: There had been friction between the two countries for a long time, but relations have improved recently.

notes:
{摩擦|まさつ} is used both literally (physical friction) and figuratively (conflict between people/groups).

Physics context:
- {摩擦|まさつ}{力|りょく} (frictional force)
- {摩擦|まさつ}{係数|けいすう} (coefficient of friction)
- {摩擦|まさつ}{熱|ねつ} (frictional heat)

Social/political context:
- {貿易|ぼうえき}{摩擦|まさつ} (trade friction)
- {国際|こくさい}{摩擦|まさつ} (international friction)
- {人間関係|にんげんかんけい}の{摩擦|まさつ} (interpersonal conflict)

Related terms:
- {衝突|しょうとつ} (collision, clash - more intense)
